objective: Preserve Pi-Agent planning autonomy while adding explicit business-policy approval, ESCI candidate admission, uncertainty-aware answerability, and bounded repair.

invariants.rule: Pi-Agent proposes the ordered TurnPlan for every natural-language turn; business policy does not become a second planner.
Business policy returns APPROVED, REPAIR_REQUIRED, or REJECTED and never silently adds, removes, or changes semantic operations.
No unapproved proposal may mutate Goal, DialogueState, WorkingSet, call a provider, or publish an assistant response.
Repair feedback identifies the violation location, observed value, and admissible alternatives within a bounded proposal budget.
Explicitly stated shopping-goal fields remain in the same approved plan when another field requires clarification; bounded repair reports all detectable omissions together.
Model, protocol, tool, and runtime failures never create user clarification.
A clear question with unknown evidence is answered by disclosure or retrieval, not by asking the user to rephrase.
Clarification is allowed only for decision-relevant intent ambiguity or missing information that the user can provide.
Every retrieved item receives an auditable Exact, Substitute, Complement, Irrelevant, or Unresolved assessment before candidate admission and ranking.
Substitutes, complements, irrelevant items, and unresolved items cannot enter the main-product recommendation cohort.
Models may infer open-world semantics, but deterministic policies own state mutation, candidate admission, clarification permission, and claim publication.
Shadow evaluation is read-only; after cutover there is one writable production execution path and no legacy runtime fallback.
Production control flow is not driven by specific user phrases, product names, or one-off category examples.
The implementation uses typed domain policies and does not introduce a generic policy or workflow DSL.
